title: lora_recv_async 4.1.0 migration: native_sim path (lora_loopback.c + lora_l2_rx.c)
description: Child 1 of 0l5j (DONE - committed as 2b37671686 on beads-worker-6; this bead is being created retroactively to fix an id/title cross in the create batch that mislabeled 0l5j.1 as the lora_sim child and wrongly closed it). Zephyr 4.x changed lora_recv_async/lora_recv_cb to carry void *user_data (v3.7.0 5-param cb at lora.h:123 vs v4.1.0 6-param) - lora_l2_rx.c (:139/:310/:380 + ISR cb + forward decl at :93) and lora_loopback.c (:239 cb invocation, :301 registration) were on the 2-arg contract and failed -Werror on v4.1.0 native_sim, blocking every ping_l2-family build. Fix: new lichen/include/lichen/lora_compat.h with version-conditional macros (LORA_RECV_ASYNC/LORA_RECV_ASYNC_1/LORA_RECV_CB_EXTRA_ARGS/LORA_RECV_CB_PASS/LORA_RECV_CB_UNUSED; same pattern as the coap_client v3.7/v4.1 lock fix), lora_l2_rx.c migrated (arm/re-arm/disarm + ISR signature), lora_loopback.c migrated (recv_user_data stored in per-instance data under the existing rx_lock span, cb invoked with it, 3-arg API fn, version-guarded store). VERIFIED: ping_l2 native_sim v4.1.0 builds clean and runs 4 pass/3 fail - exactly the pre-existing 5fva-family baseline, no panic, no recv_async regression. NOTE: orphaned commit f0a661c182 on another branch holds a lora_compat.h byte-identical to this one (independent convergence; header merge is a no-op). An identical header text was also what the mislabeled 0l5j.1 briefly carried - now correctly attributed here.
close_reason: Done and committed as 2b37671686 'fix(l2): lora_recv_async 4.1.0 contract on native_sim path' on beads-worker-6 (created retroactively to repair the id/title cross that briefly mislabeled 0l5j.1). Verification: ping_l2 native_sim v4.1.0 builds with ZERO recv_async errors (previously 3 TUs failing) and runs 4 pass/3 fail - exactly the pre-existing 5fva-family baseline, no panic; the passing set includes the RX arm/disarm/retry lifecycle tests, so the migrated loopback + l2_rx path is exercised. 3x kimi-k3 review passes consumed the diff (two outputs clipped by tool timeouts, one completed PASS); my own line-audit: macro double-eval safe (dev/cb single lvalues), empty-expansion safe, guarded store inside the existing rx_lock span, no missed call sites (grep: lora_l2_rx.c is the only lora_recv_async caller outside the drivers). Siblings 0l5j.2 (renode)/0l5j.3 (lr1110) remain open; 0l5j.1 (lora_sim) reopened after the mis-close.
